unique_contract_reads.MaxHTLC/MinHTLC: all four routers read these (not a differentiator)

machinery_built: remainingFeeBudget() = FeeLimitMsat - committedFees - budgetGuard; committedFees accrues only on SETTLED shards
tryAllocation splits the remaining budget proportionally per shard (shardCap = remaining*shard/remainingAmount + min(remaining/20,25k) rounding allowance) and decrements after each shard
findRoute prunes on totalFee>feeCap INSIDE the Dijkstra, plus a post-check; budget is a search constraint, not a filter
riskPrice(feeCap): the fee/reliability exchange rate is budget-derived (feeCap/2 clamped to [30k,420k] msat per nat of -log p)
maxLabelsPerNode=8 multi-label Pareto search over (score,fee,amount) that never evicts the minimum-FEE label - keeps a cheap feasible path in the frontier when the budget binds
budgetGuard: reserve of max(fee/20,1000) added on an UNATTRIBUTED failure when a finite limit exists
nodeFee(in,out,amt) = outbound fee + inbound base/rate with a floor-at-zero clamp; used in search AND in buildRoute's amount ladder
reserved map: own-shard cumulative load, checked against capacity and local balance and used as the belief index (loads, not amounts)
reusedEdgeCostMsat=1.1M disjointness pressure (x0.55 on source edges); extraPartCostMsat=45k per extra shard

TWO-TIER belief ledger: process-global sharedBeliefs with SOFT failure evidence (0.012, justified in-comment by concurrent depletion) vs a payment-local strict localUpper + retryCutoff (3/4, or 1/2 after 3 fails) - the exp-018 dual-ledger idea realized
confidence time-decay exp(-age/1800s) - re-invents the decay hb1/mx_c3 dropped
blocked set: CodeFeeInsufficient/CodeIncorrectCltvExpiry treated as deterministic policy mismatch, hard-blocked, and explicitly NOT written into liquidity beliefs
unattributed failure = soft +500k penalty on every hop, not a route nuke (aligns with exp-021 soft_unknown)

caps.note: econ2's fixed cap is the LOWEST of the fixed-cap routers, so the harness attempt-ceiling escape is not open wider for it

defect_found.econ2: exp-025-econ2-best-candidate.go:79 nodeFee: inbound = base + amt*rate/1e6  (amt only, outFee omitted)
defect_found.effect: systematically underpays a POSITIVE inbound fee by outFee*inboundRate/1e6, which the forwarding node refuses with CodeFeeInsufficient
defect_found.wire: econ2 logs 13.0 inbound_fee_refusals/file on b_heavy and 8.08 on econ_test where lnd logs zero
defect_found.scope: bites the heavy family's 43.2 surcharge policies/file, not its 1421.6 discounts

H-C2.source: tracks budget across shards (committedFees on settle, proportional per-shard split, decrement), re-plans (plan nil'd on every failure + queuedAmount mismatch), and makes the search price budget-derived via riskPrice() and a fee-Pareto label set - this is NOT merely a lowered fee weight
H-C2.wire: fee_limit_failures = 0 on ALL SIX budgeted tiers, matching lnd exactly. seed 22-644/file, hb1 9.9-291, mx_c3 9.9-220, atomic1 8.6-62.5. First evolved candidate ever to report zero.
H-C2.outcome: fee_budget family: CI-excluding-zero wins over lnd 4/4, hb1 4/4, mx_c3 3/4, atomic1 3/4; cap-robust

H-B1.source: reads ch.InboundFee; nodeFee prices inbound base+rate with correct floor-at-zero, in both the search and the amount ladder
H-B1.wire: b_heavy fee_ppm 283.5 vs lnd 320.1 and champions 2814-4829 - econ2 is the only candidate that prices routes like lnd. But inbound_fee_refusals 13.0/file vs lnd's 0 (see defect_found).
H-B1.outcome: b_heavy: beats lnd (+0.091) and seed (+0.093) with CIs excluding zero; vs champions +0.028..+0.050, all straddling zero - the fee saving is real but the objective's fee term is capped at 0.1, so it converts weakly

H-A1.source: usableHTLC() filters min/max HTLC and capacity at plan time - but so do all three champions (all read MaxHTLC/MinHTLC)
H-A1.wire: htlc_max/min/source_refusals are ZERO for EVERY router on a_tight and econ_test - exp-023 stage A's plan-time finding reproduces, so the counter cannot discriminate
H-A1.outcome: a_tight is econ2's WORST relative tier: -0.103 vs hb1 and -0.104 vs mx_c3, both CIs excluding zero. No sizing-against-caps advantage exists.

H-D1.verdict: PARTIAL - real machinery, no objective win
H-D1.source: reserved-load accounting + reused-edge disjointness pressure + joint route-set planning + the two-tier soft/strict belief ledger
H-D1.wire: self_contention_failures 5.85 (d_w2) / 14.55 (d_w4) vs hb1 17.75/40.45, mx_c3 6.85/16.60, lnd 56.35/88.50 - second only to atomic1's 0.35/2.85
H-D1.outcome: concurrency family: 0 CI-excluding-zero wins over mx_c3 or atomic1 at any window; beats lnd 3/3 and hb1 at w4 only. The contention machinery works and does not convert.

verdict.criteria: champion displacement needs a CI-excluding-zero win over a champion on the tier family claimed; an econ-world-only lead with clean-tier losses files it as the economic-world specialist
verdict.recommendation: ECONOMIC-WORLD SPECIALIST - specifically the FEE-BUDGET specialist. NOT a champion displacement.
verdict.for: CI-excluding-zero wins over hb1 on 4/4 fee-budget tiers, mx_c3 3/4, atomic1 3/4, and over all three champions on the held-out econ_test. Unanimous on c_mn_100 (hb1 10/0 p=.0020, mx_c3 10/0 p=.0020). Cap-robust on the fee family (uncapped means +0.176/+0.123/+0.067).
verdict.against: loses the classic sealed set: hb1 4L/1W, mx_c3 4L/0W over six tiers; loses 2-3 of the four econ CONTROL tiers to hb1/mx_c3; worst candidate on a_tight. Champions keep the generalist title.

beat_lnd_on_econ.claim: YES - a program first, stated regardless
beat_lnd_on_econ.econ_test: +0.0478, 16/4 p=.0118; the cap-15 CI [-0.0020,0.1035] straddles zero by 0.002; uncapped +0.1975 with CI excluding zero
beat_lnd_on_econ.significance: exp-023 found the champions' clean-mainnet lead goes NEGATIVE at every fee rung (reproduced here: hb1 0.570 and mx_c3 0.601 vs lnd 0.627 at 400 ppm). econ2 restores an lnd-beating lead on exactly those rungs: 0.721 at 400 and 0.664 at 100, best of all six routers.

cap_check.verdict: the econ_test champion lead is MOSTLY a cap subsidy; the fee-budget family lead is NOT
cap_check.econ_test: vs hb1 +0.109 -> +0.048 uncapped (56% of the margin was cap subsidy); mx_c3 +0.101 -> +0.032 (68%); atomic1 +0.106 -> +0.029 (73%). Sign flips nowhere - econ2 also wins econ_test on raw SUCCESS (+0.126/+0.113/+0.146) and on fees (630 vs 1625-1795 ppm) - but the CIs stop excluding zero once attempts are priced in full. econ2 spends 21.4 att/pmt there against the champions' 7-12.
cap_check.fee_budget: c_2000 is IDENTICAL at every cap (+0.093/+0.067/+0.119, econ2 at 5.4 att/pmt is below saturation); c_mn_400 and c_mn_100 GROW uncapped. No subsidy.
cap_check.ceiling_escape: econ2's maxRouterAttempts=72 is below hb1's 96 and mx_c3's 80, so the exp-022 inverse attractor is not open wider for it; and give_up_rate == 1-success_rate holds exactly for econ2 on all 21 tiers, so give-ups carry no independent abandonment signal (exp-017's rule; read the success/attempt pair)

anomalies: econ2's single worst tier is gate_drift_test: -0.160 vs hb1, -0.171 vs mx_c3, and -0.131 vs the SEED, at 24.1 att/pmt. The corpus-econ README pre-registers the cause: the composition world is 'a low-drift, high-contention world' (5s arrival gap replaces the 600s payment gap), so econ2 never bred against staleness.

the give_up_rate == 1-success_rate identity holds for all four evolved candidates but NOT for the hand-written seed on the economic tiers (deviations to 0.56) - exp-017's 'style fingerprint' is candidate-specific, not universal
seed beats econ2 on c_4000 (0.444 vs 0.434) and is the strongest non-lnd router on several econ controls

b_heavy: econ2 saves ~4150 fee ppm against the champions yet gains only +0.03..+0.05 objective, because the fee term saturates at 5000 ppm (max penalty 0.1) - the objective cannot see most of the saving
